The Charles Stanley Female Founders 2024 report
provides an analysis of the landscape for women-led
businesses in the UK. It examines the impact of female
founders, their contributions to the economy, and the
barriers they continue to face—particularly in securing
equity investment.
The report explores key trends in female
entrepreneurship, including founder demographics, key
industries, and investment trends. It highlights the
persistent funding gap, where male-led businesses
secured over six times the equity investment raised by
female-founded companies in 2024. It also examines
the role of mentorship, investor diversity, and support
networks in driving change.
Through case studies and survey insights, the report
sheds light on female entrepreneurs’ experiences—
from launching their first ventures to scaling and
exiting businesses. It provides a deeper understanding
of the challenges faced by women in securing funding,
navigating industry biases, and accessing the networks

About the authors
Henry Whorwood
Managing Director

Henry leads our Research & Consultancy
team, and is an expert on equity finance and
high-growth business. He's worked on briefs
for the likes of Barclays, SyndicateRoom,
Innovate UK, Smith & Williamson and British
Business Bank. He regularly gives
presentations on market trends at events
around the UK.
Callum Newton
Senior Associate

Callum is a Senior Research & Consultancy
Associate, responsible for leading on the
team's public sector work. Before joining
Beauhurst, Callum was a Senior Researcher
at Westminster-based think-tank Onward
focusing on ‘Levelling Up’ policy. He was
also a Consultant in Portland
Communication’s specialist Litigation &
Disputes practice.
